Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — OmniRetail is excited about Redwood's latency and cost controls. A couple of procurement questions before we share the forecast with finance:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood applies per-token volume breakpoints as marginal (only the tokens above the breakpoint get the lower rate) or blended (the lower rate applies to ALL prior tokens once you hit the breakpoint)? Our CFO is trying to model worst-case vs expected spend.

2) We operate in NA and EU regions. If we hit the top breakpoint in NA but not in EU, is the ladder applied per-region or across the account (single aggregated ladder)?

3) Procurement also asked for an example invoice showing how discounts would show up across regions. I attached our high-level forecast.

If you can send a short worked example and the formal pricing schedule, that would help speed approval.

Best,

Hi Andre — great questions, thanks for sending the forecast. Quick answers up top, then a short worked example below:

- Short answer on ladder semantics: Redwood supports both models, but our standard hosted API per-token ladder is marginal by default. That means each token is billed at the marginal rate for the bucket it falls into.
- Cross-region behavior: by default we aggregate usage across the account and apply a single ladder. If you prefer separate ladders per region (so NA and EU never share breakpoints), we can create partitioned committed pools. Partitioning is possible but does change how committed discounts and capacity guarantees are structured.

Worked example (simplified):
- Breakpoints: 0-10M @ $0.00008, next 10M @ $0.00006, >20M @ $0.000045 (marginal)
- If you use 25M tokens total in a billing period: 10M @ .00008 + 10M @ .00006 + 5M @ .000045 = blended effective rate ~$0.000064 per token.

I'll attach our formal pricing tiers PDF and an example invoice calc. Laura — looping you in for the committed-tier options and to note the partitioning tradeoffs.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher

Andre — thanks for the clear asks. Apologies for the length; wanted to make the examples explicit for procurement/finance.

On ladder timing: our hosted API ladder is evaluated per billing period (calendar month by default). We can support trailing-30-day aggregation for special contracts, but that requires an SLA/commit change and different overage handling.

Attached are two artifacts: Committed_Capacity_Options.pdf (shows partitioned vs aggregated pools) and Example_Invoice_Calc.csv (worked numbers). Summary of the relevant pieces below.

Example A — Aggregated (default):
- Account uses NA: 12M tokens, EU: 6M tokens = 18M tokens aggregated
- Pricing ladder (example): 0-10M @ $0.00010, next 10M @ $0.00007, >20M @ $0.00005 (marginal)
- Billing calc (marginal): 10M @ .00010 + 8M @ .00007 = $1,000 + $560 = $1,560 -> effective rate $0.0000867/token
- Billing calc (blended if forced): 18M @ $0.00007 = $1,260 -> effective rate $0.00007/token (note: blended benefits the buyer once breakpoint reached)

Example B — Partitioned pools (NA and EU separate):
- NA 12M -> 10M @ .00010 + 2M @ .00007 = $1,000 + $140 = $1,140 (eff rate .000095)
- EU 6M -> 6M @ .00010 = $600 (eff rate .00010)
- Combined invoice = $1,740 (higher than aggregated marginal outcome)

Recommendation: For OmniRetail's forecast (high NA skew) aggregated laddering gives better economics and is simpler operationally. Partitioned pools are helpful if you need independent capacity guarantees or strict regional cost attribution.

PoC credits / payment terms:
- We can offer a one-time $10k proof-of-concept credit for a 3-month pilot when you sign an intent-to-commit and Net-30 payment term is acceptable for the post-PoC contract.
- We'll document that credit in the SOW/Order Form (reduces first invoice).

Breakpoints: We typically negotiate two levers: breakpoints (token thresholds) and marginal step sizes (the $/token differential). We're flexible on shifting the top breakpoint lower if you need to hit a higher marginal discount earlier.

Attachments: Committed_Capacity_Options.pdf, Example_Invoice_Calc.csv
